summary:
Space Mission Simulator is an interactive educational game designed to help students understand the process of planning and carrying out space missions through hands-on experience rather than theory alone.
Players take on the role of a mission planner, choose between Moon and Mars exploration, and design their own spacecraft by selecting components and managing fuel, power, and mass. NASA data is used as a reference for spacecraft design and component selection, helping determine whether a mission succeeds or fails in the simulation.
We developed a playable prototype that takes players through spacecraft assembly, launch, and mission evaluation. The game has been tested with four players, with both successful and unsuccessful mission outcomes.
Although the current version still has limitations in data accuracy and interface design, it provides a starting point for making space science more accessible and engaging. Our next goal is to improve the accuracy of the data and develop a more intuitive 3D experience.
details:
SPACE MISSION SIMULATOR is an interactive educational game developed to make space mission design easier to understand and more engaging for students. Our idea came from a simple observation: technical information about space missions and NASA's scientific data can be difficult for students to understand when presented mainly through theory. We wanted to turn these complex concepts into an experience where learners can explore, make decisions, and see the consequences of their choices.

In the game, players take on the role of a space mission planner and go through the main stages of a mission. First, they choose their exploration destination: the Moon or Mars. They then design and assemble a spacecraft by selecting different components. During this process, players need to consider important resources such as fuel, electrical power, and total spacecraft mass. Once the spacecraft is assembled, they proceed to launch and observe the mission simulation. The game then displays whether the mission succeeds or fails based on the design and choices made by the player.

NASA data is used as a reference for spacecraft design and component selection. It helps us build the technical foundation of the game and connect the learning experience with real-world space exploration. Rather than simply presenting scientific information, we aim to let players interact with mission-related parameters and understand why different design decisions matter.

The main benefit of the project is its hands-on approach to learning. Students can explore space mission concepts through experimentation instead of relying only on textbooks or theoretical explanations. Both successful and unsuccessful outcomes are part of the experience, allowing players to learn from their decisions and better understand the challenges involved in planning a space mission.

We have developed a playable prototype and tested it with four players. The testing produced both successful and unsuccessful mission outcomes, showing that players could experience different results through the game. However, the current version still has limitations. The interface needs to become more intuitive and visually engaging, and some of the data used in the simulation still needs further verification and improvement.

Our next steps are to improve the accuracy of the data used for spacecraft design and develop a more intuitive 3D interface. In the long term, we hope to make space science more accessible and inspire more students to explore science, technology, engineering, and space exploration through interactive learning.

SPACE MISSION SIMULATOR is our first step toward turning the complexity of space mission design into an experience that students can explore for themselves.
